channel.title: Glass Power Tools
channel.description: Glass Power Tools for Mac updates

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.616
item.description:
0.4.616

  • A terminal that loses its connection says so in the window. Its text dims under a panel with the reason, Reconnect and Close Terminal; while it reconnects on its own, each try. Close Terminal closes a disconnected terminal's pane, rather than leaving it saying the session ended.
  • A machine asleep or away is found out once, not once per terminal. The app waits 15 seconds for an answer, and a machine's other terminals take the first one's answer: "name didn't answer. It may be asleep, or off the network."
  • Tailscale off, said at once. A machine at a Tailscale address while Tailscale is off on this Mac says Tailscale Is Off, rather than waiting out the connection; for terminals, remote desktops and databases.
  • The Dock icon counts the terminals that rang their bell where you can't see them, on another desktop or covered; or a notification names one, or both (Settings ▸ Connections). The app asks once for permission to show them, as it starts.
  • Edit the line as on a Mac. ⌥← / ⌥→ move a word, ⌘← / ⌘→ go to the line's start and end, ⌥⌫ / ⌥⌦ delete a word, ⌘⌫ back to the start, and ⌥-click puts the cursor where you click, as in Apple's Terminal.

Everything in this build: the release notes.

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.612
item.description:
0.4.612

  • Suggestions as you type. At a shell prompt the terminal offers the rest of the command in grey after the cursor: → takes all of it, ⌥→ its next word. They come from what you've run on that machine, your snippets and library, the folder you're in, paths as you type them, common tools and the machine's programs, and what you run stays on this Mac. Settings ▸ Suggestions sets them; a terminal on a server needs the shell integration installed there, from the same page.
  • Every SSH terminal has its folder button. Open Folder Here opens the folder the shell is in, read from its prompt's title on Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Arch, and Files at home when the shell doesn't say.
  • A paste is text, never keys. Control characters hidden in copied text are left out, as xterm leaves them out, so a paste can't end itself early and run what follows.
  • ⌘V pastes a picture into a terminal as dropping it does: saved, or uploaded on a server, and its path typed.
  • Two machines at one address stay two machines, such as two sites on one server; they were folded into one.
  • Resizing a tab in tmux no longer fills it with copies of the prompt, and Scale Text works in a local tab in tmux.

Everything in this build: the release notes.

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.603
item.description:
0.4.603

  • The orbs are drops of liquid. A window landing in the orb dock squashes and wobbles like jelly until it settles, and the orbs beside it feel it in turn; the dock's glass stretches past its new size and springs back. A busy terminal's orb has drops falling into it, rings of ripples spreading across its picture. Reduce Motion or Low Power Mode keeps them still.
  • The dock is a row or a column (Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Orbs ▸ Dock), and keeps the length you drag it to: longer shows more orbs, shorter fewer, to whole orbs. A window docked again goes back into its row.
  • Undo and redo in the Editor, named as TextEdit names them, and the Editor's Edit menu is TextEdit's: Find and Replace, Use Selection for Find, Paste and Match Style, Spelling and Grammar, Substitutions, Transformations and Speech.
  • A terminal that rings its bell while you're not looking stays marked in orange, in its tab, its orb and Show All Windows, until you go to it.

Everything in this build: the release notes.

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.589
item.description:
0.4.589

  • The orb dock. Shrink to Orb, in every window's toolbar beside Show All Windows, puts the window in a dock of glass orbs that floats over your windows, its sessions still running. Each terminal window's orb shows the tab in front, with its tabs as dots around it in their coding agents' colours; databases, desktops and editors gather on their machine's orb; Connections comes first, with Active's count. Click an orb to bring its window back, or a dot for that tab; drag one orb onto another to reorder them. The dock is Apple's Liquid Glass and grows from Connections as orbs arrive. Choose where it floats, and its Opacity and Glass, in Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Orbs. ⌘M still minimizes to the Mac's Dock.
  • Terminal Overview (⌥⌘G) looks like Show All Windows, inside the window, with that window's tabs: live tiles, type to find, the arrow keys and Return. Carousel, beside Grid, shows the tabs as an album view: one large in front, the rest turned toward it, a trackpad swipe moving the row. The old Terminal Carousel (⌥⇧⌘G) is gone.
  • Shrink to Orb is a circle everywhere a window becomes one.
  • ⌫ takes back a letter of what you typed in Show All Windows. A terminal that can't connect as it is shown says why. No dark crescents in a rounded window's corners.

Everything in this build: the release notes.

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.575
item.description:
0.4.575

  • Databases and remote desktops in Workgroups. A Workgroup can open databases and remote desktops from your library with its terminals, or on their own. Add them in the Workgroup's editor under Databases and Desktops; each opens as Connect opens it, and one already open comes forward instead of connecting again.
  • New Glass Power Tools Tab Here is a Finder Quick Action, beside Window Here: right-click a folder ▸ Quick Actions, or the Finder's preview pane. macOS leaves a new Quick Action off; if one is missing, turn it on in Quick Actions ▸ Customize….
  • Favorites name a service by its machine when its name says nothing more ("Database on alpha" shows as alpha, Database).

Everything in this build: the release notes.

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.569
item.description:
0.4.569

  • Git, end to end, in the editor. History with its graph, branches, stashes and tags, merges and rebases with a conflict resolver, blame, and cloning. Diffs follow Wrap Long Lines, Show Only Changed Files narrows the tree, and the tree marks deleted, conflicted, staged and ignored files and says where a rename came from. It needs Git 2.16 or later.
  • Follow a log. Right-click a log file's path in a terminal and Watch Log File comes first: it follows the log in a new tab. Its preview keeps up as it grows when the log is on this Mac. Open in Preview opens a picture or a PDF a terminal names, and a path's closing punctuation is left off.
  • Workgroups across Macs. A workgroup's local terminals belong to their Mac; your other devices, another Mac too, open them there over SSH, on their own tmux sessions.
  • One ⚡ on every terminal toolbar for Active. Split Right and Split Down are in each pane's gear menu, and Open Folder in Editor works from a terminal window.
  • Faster terminals: only the rows that changed are drawn again.
  • Editor windows show as pictures in Show All Windows and the switcher.
  • Changing an SSH key on one device no longer removes the key records another device made. The library's iCloud line says what to do: "Sign in to iCloud to sync", or "Check iCloud to sync".

Everything in this build: the release notes.

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.548
item.description:
0.4.548

  • Terminal color schemes. Import macOS Terminal profiles (.terminal files, or a folder of them) and choose among them in a terminal's Settings ▸ All Terminals ▸ Theme ▸ Choose…, each shown in its own colors. They're kept in iCloud Drive ▸ Glass Power Tools ▸ Terminal Themes for every device, and This Window can use one too. Background, text, selection, cursor and all sixteen colors come across; your font stays. Open With Glass Power Tools on a .terminal file adds it.
  • Git in the editor. A project's branch at the foot of its files, a Changes tab, change marks beside the lines, staging and committing, and now Pull, Push, Fetch and Publish Branch, with plain words when one can't go ahead.
  • Four more terminal looks: Coding Agent, Aurora, Starfield and Blueprint. A Workgroup can have a look of its own.
  • Mermaid diagrams a program prints in a terminal, as Claude Code does, are marked and open as pictures. Tabs show the coding agent they're running.
  • New terminals from the sidebar: right-click its empty space for what the toolbar's + offers.
  • ⌘F finds in the editor, with Find Next and Find Previous.
  • A database that won't connect says why, and its Connection Details show where the tunnel goes. A remote desktop that ends the session says why.
  • A Files window opened on an empty folder fills the window, instead of a message floating in clear glass.
  • Saved connections changed on another device stay changed. Cancel and the time limit stop any SQLite query. A tmux server the app started can be stopped.

Everything in this build: the release notes.

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.494
item.description:
0.4.494

  • Scale Text works on this Mac's own terminals, tmux tabs included.
  • Open Folder in Editor, in a terminal's gear menu: the project that holds the shell's folder, or a new editor window.
  • A local terminal's gear menu no longer repeats the toolbar's buttons.
  • A Mac signed out of iCloud says so, and how to sign in, instead of "iCloud sync failed".

item.title: Glass Power Tools 0.4.491
item.description:
The first Mac release

  • Your Library counts the time you spend on each machine.
  • A Mac recognises its own record in the library.
  • Looks for terminal windows: Digital Rain, Synthwave, phosphor, pictures, glow.
  • Right-click SQL in a terminal to open it in the query editor.
  • tmux tabs keep every line.
